parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two capacitors, of capacitances $C_1$ and $C_2$, are connected in parallel to a power supply of electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E$, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1.png}}

Fig. 5.1

Show that the combined capacitance $C_T$ of the two capacitors is given by

$$C_T = C_1 + C_2.$$

Explain your reasoning. You may draw on Fig. 5.1 if you wish.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Two capacitors of capacitances $22\,\mu\text{F}$ and $47\,\mu\text{F}$, and a resistor of resistance $2.7\,\text{M}\Omega$, are connected into the circuit of Fig. 5.2.

{{figure:figure_5_2.png}}

Fig. 5.2

The battery has an e.m.f. of $12\text{V}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Show that the combined capacitance of the two capacitors is $15\,\mu\text{F}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The two-way switch $S$ is initially at position $X$, so that the capacitors are fully charged.

Use the information in (c)(i) to calculate the total energy stored in the two capacitors.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The two-way switch is now moved to position $Y$.

Determine the time taken for the potential difference (p.d.) across the $22\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor to become $6.0\text{V}$.
